analyzed_vuln.description: For an in-memory frame, `frame_get_lazychunk` computes `frame->cframe + header_len + offset` and trusts the embedded chunk's `cbytes` field without verifying that the complete chunk lies within `frame->len` (and without robustly validating the `header_len + offset` sum). It returns this attacker-controlled claimed size to `blosc2_decompress_ctx`. Consequently, `blosc_d` treats an out-of-frame block-start offset as in bounds relative to the fictitious `srcsize`, advances `src` to a wild address, and crashes when `sw32_` reads the stream size at blosc2.c:1344.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The input must parse as an in-memory contiguous frame with at least enough declared chunks for the harness to decompress one. Its compressed-offset table must select an embedded chunk whose header is reachable, while that chunk declares a `cbytes`/source extent larger than the bytes actually remaining in the frame. A malicious block-start entry that is outside the real frame but below the falsely trusted `cbytes` then passes `blosc_d`'s `src_offset < srcsize` check. The harness passes the frame buffer to `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer`, then `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk`; `frame_get_lazychunk` propagates the unbounded chunk pointer and claimed length to decompression, producing the wild read.

args: In c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c, analyze frame_get_lazychunk() for an in-memory contiguous frame. What exact boundary and integer-overflow checks should be made before forming frame->cframe + header_len + offset, reading BLOSC2_CHUNK_CBYTES, and returning that claimed chunk size? Note any relevant constants and expected error codes, and whether frame->len or parsed frame_len should be authoritative.

The supplied ASan crash occurs because frame_get_lazychunk at c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c:1972 forms an embedded chunk pointer and reads its cbytes field, then returns the attacker-declared cbytes to frame_decompress_chunk and blosc2_decompress_ctx. The compressed-offset entry reaches a chunk header, but the claimed chunk extent exceeds the actual in-memory frame. get_coffset only checks offset > frame->len and ignores header_len addition. I am considering subtraction-based checks against frame->len: validate header_len and offset, ensure enough bytes remain to read the minimum/header cbytes field, decode cbytes, and ensure it is no larger than the remaining bytes. I want this rooted at the in-memory lazychunk branch while preserving disk/sparse frame behavior.
